```

## What mine does that `list_leagues.py` does not

That script prints league names. Mine pulls **the data you actually need**: metadata, settings, standings, teams, draft results, transactions, scoreboard, weekly matchups, and **per-team weekly roster player stats** — the last one being the endpoint that closes the bonus gap. All 14 league IDs are wired, into immutable `raw/yahoo/<season>/`.

I just enabled token persistence (`env_file_location` + `save_token_data_to_env_file=True`), so run 4 will not re-prompt.

## Watch the consent screen

The other Claude is right that the Fantasy Sports checkbox is gone from Yahoo's app form, and right that the scope most likely arrives at consent time instead. **Read what the Allow screen says it is granting.** If it never mentions fantasy data, or step 3 returns 401/403, that is the cause and we go back to app settings.

**Your 2017 entry is still contradictory** — ID `351067` but the URL points at `/2017/f1/701692`. My script has `351067`. Step 3 will tell us: if 2017 fails and every other season works, the URL was right and I will flip it.

## The 5% is six long-play bonuses

Your league paid extra for explosive plays, every Yahoo year 2013-2024. Sleeper dropped them in 2025.

| Stat | Bonus |
|---|---|
| 40+ yard completion | **+1** |
| 40+ yard passing TD | **+2** |
| 40+ yard rush | **+1** |
| 40+ yard rushing TD | **+2** |
| 40+ yard reception | **+1** |
| 40+ yard receiving TD | **+2** |

Confirmed present in 2013, 2020, and 2024. **Zero in 2025.**

## Where they went missing

LeagueLegacy kept them in the **team total** but stripped them from the **per-player rows**. Your own week, 2013 week 1:

| Player | Yahoo | LeagueLegacy | Lost |
|---|---|---|---|
| Aaron Rodgers | 30.62 | 24.62 | **6.00** |
| A.J. Green | 41.20 | 37.20 | **4.00** |
| Steven Jackson | 18.20 | 17.20 | **1.00** |
| Six others | same | same | 0 |
| **Total** | **150.62** | 139.62 | **11.00** |

Rodgers threw three 40-yard TDs. Green caught two deep balls, one for a score. Jackson broke one 40-yard run. The archive shows none of it at player level.

**6.14 points per team-week on average. 4.99% of scoring. 2,256 team-weeks.**

## What you need to get me

**Per-player weekly points from Yahoo, seasons 2013-2024.** That is it. One endpoint: `get_team_roster_player_stats_by_week`. Already wired in `src/fetch_yahoo.py`.

**Your two remaining actions:**
1. Paste the Client ID and Secret into the nano window that is still open
2. Click Allow on the browser consent screen and paste the verification code

Then I run all twelve seasons unattended.

Nothing else is missing. Draft picks, transactions, standings, champions, identity, lineage — all complete and verified.

**It matters for:** per-pick value. The bonuses land almost entirely on deep-threat receivers, explosive backs, and vertical quarterbacks — which is exactly the player archetype Phase 3 is trying to measure. If Chris & Dom won by drafting big-play receivers, the current data systematically understates them. That is a bias, not noise.

| | |
|---|---|

| **Phase 5, your 2026 draft** | **Uses none of it.** Runs on current projections |

### Claude - 2026-08-11 17:02:46

Definitive answer, and it is not good.

## The Yahoo API path is closed

`oauth_problem="additional_authorization_required"` means the token is valid but **the app has no Fantasy Sports scope.** I checked both of your apps:

| App | Permission options available |
|---|---|
| `yfpy-fantasy-app` | OpenID Connect (Email, Profile), TW Auction |
| `Fantasy Football League - Historical Analyzer` | OpenID Connect (Email, Profile), TW Auction |

**Fantasy Sports does not appear anywhere in Yahoo's developer console.** Not on the create form, not on either app's settings page. It cannot be added post-creation.

Yahoo's own docs now say new apps must **apply for access** — submit your organization, product, and use case, wait for review and approval. It is no longer a checkbox. That is why every yfpy tutorial says "check the Fantasy Sports box" and no such box exists.

So: creating another app will not help, and neither will ChatGPT finding a different library. **Every Python wrapper — yfpy, yahoofantasy, all of them — hits this same wall**, because the wall is on Yahoo's side of the OAuth grant, not in the code.

## What still works

**The Chrome scrape.** I already proved it end to end: 2013 weeks 1-7 pulled clean, 2,464 rows, zero errors, with **bonus-inclusive per-player points** — the exact data the API was going to give us. Two obstacles, both just slow rather than blocking:

| Obstacle | Handling |
|---|---|
| HTTP 999 after ~50 fetches | Pace at ~40 per window with backoff |
| Extraction bandwidth | `get_page_text` moves ~900 rows per call |

Roughly 1,000 fetches total across twelve seasons. It is hours, not minutes, and it is fragile — but it is a path that exists, versus one that does not.

## My recommendation

**Delete both Yahoo apps now.** They grant nothing, and one of their secrets is in this chat. There is no reason to leave them standing.

Then pick one:

**A — accept the 5%.** Phases 2, 3, and 4 run today on a stated basis. Your September 8 draft uses none of it. The bonus is 4.99% of scoring and flips 4.17% of historical games.

**B — apply to Yahoo.** Legitimate long-term fix, unknown turnaround, almost certainly not before September 8.

**C — grind the scrape.** I pace it across many turns, most recent seasons first. Real, proven, slow.

I would take **A now and B in parallel** — start the application, and if it is ever approved the historical correction backfills cleanly. The draft does not wait on either.

Sources: [Yahoo Fantasy Sports API guide](https://developer.yahoo.com/fantasysports/guide/), [yahoofantasy on PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/yahoofantasy/1.4.5), [YahooFantasyWrapper](https://github.com/isaacrlevin/YahooFantasyWrapper)

## The central number

**68.9% of starter points come from drafted players.** This league is won on draft day roughly two-thirds, bought after it one-third. Stable across twelve seasons, ranging 60.2% to 76.2%.

## But it does not predict winning

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| corr(drafted share, finish rank) | **-0.124** |
| corr(drafted share, champion) | **+0.055** |
| Champions mean share | 71.6% (n=13) |
| Non-champions mean share | 68.8% (n=143) |
| Difference | **+2.9 points** |

Both correlations are near zero on 156 franchise-seasons. **Drafting well relative to waivers is not what separates champions here.**

## And the number that should stop you

| Franchise | Drafted share | Titles |
|---|---|---|
| Rob & GregBo | **81.2%** — highest in the league | 1 |
| Phil Baldino | 72.3% | **3** |
| **Cambrias** | **65.2%** | **3** |
| **Antdell & Ernie** | **65.4%** | **0** |

**You and Cambria have effectively the same drafted-versus-acquired profile — 65.4% against 65.2%.** Same balance of draft capital and in-season acquisition. He has three rings and you have none.

Whatever separates you from the best franchise in this league, **it is not how much of your production comes from the draft.** That hypothesis is dead, and killing it early is worth more than a 5% points correction would have been.

Your two three-time champions also sit at opposite ends — Baldino draft-heavy at 72.3%, Cambria waiver-leaning at 65.2%. Two different routes to the same result, consistent with the all-play split from earlier: Cambria wins on raw strength, Baldino outperforms his all-play record.

## One correction to my own gap register

I flagged G-003 saying 2013 could not support this split because transactions start in 2014. **That was wrong.** The method derives ownership from the draft record, not from transactions — a started player is either on that franchise's draft sheet or it is not. 2013 computes fine at 70.3%. All thirteen seasons are valid.

## Where Phase 3 now has to look

Not at drafted share. The live candidates are **which players get drafted** rather than how many, positional archetype in rounds 1-5, and whether Cambria's edge shows up in-season rather than on draft day.

Say the word and I run Phase 3 against all 156 franchise-seasons with the permutation test and luck controls.

ROCCI wrapper, RISEN internals. A handoff has one job the original work does not: preventing the successor from re-deriving settled facts or re-walking dead ends. | The successor inherits the accepted 5 percent basis rather than re-attempting Yahoo | Say "retry Yahoo" and I will add the application path |

# Prompt Improver Skill

## Purpose

Transform vague, ambiguous prompts into actionable, well-defined requests through systematic research and targeted clarification. This skill is invoked when the hook has already determined a prompt needs enrichment.

## When This Skill is Invoked

**Automatic invocation:**
- UserPromptSubmit hook evaluates prompt
- Hook determines prompt is vague (missing specifics, context, or clear target)
- Hook invokes this skill to guide research and questioning

**Manual invocation:**
- To enrich a vague prompt with research-based questions
- When building or testing prompt evaluation systems
- When prompt lacks sufficient context even with conversation history

**Assumptions:**
- Prompt has already been identified as vague
- Evaluation phase is complete (done by hook)
- Proceed directly to research and clarification

## Core Workflow

This skill follows a 4-phase approach to prompt enrichment:

### Phase 1: Research

Create a dynamic research plan using TodoWrite before asking questions.

**Research Plan Template:**
1. **Check conversation history first** - Avoid redundant exploration if context already exists
2. **Review codebase** if needed:
   - Task/Explore for architecture and project structure
   - Grep/Glob for specific patterns, related files
   - Check git log for recent changes
   - Search for errors, failing tests, TODO/FIXME comments
3. **Gather additional context** as needed:
   - Read local documentation files
   - WebFetch for online documentation
   - WebSearch for best practices, common approaches, current information
4. **Document findings** to ground questions in actual project context

**Critical Rules:**
- NEVER skip research
- Check conversation history before exploring codebase
- Questions must be grounded in actual findings, not assumptions or base knowledge
- Route Glob, Grep, WebSearch, WebFetch, and multi-file Read through `Task/Explore` — never call them directly in main context
- Include conversation-relevant context (file paths, errors, prior decisions) in every Explore prompt — Explore cannot see prior turns

For detailed research strategies, patterns, and examples, see [references/research-strategies.md](references/research-strategies.md).

### Phase 2: Generate Targeted Questions

Based on research findings, formulate 1-6 questions that will clarify the ambiguity.

**Question Guidelines:**
- **Grounded**: Every option comes from research (codebase findings, documentation, common patterns)
- **Specific**: Avoid vague options like "Other approach"
- **Multiple choice**: Provide 2-4 concrete options per question
- **Focused**: Each question addresses one decision point
- **Contextual**: Include brief explanations of trade-offs

**Number of Questions:**
- **1-2 questions**: Simple ambiguity (which file? which approach?)
- **3-4 questions**: Moderate complexity (scope + approach + validation)
- **5-6 questions**: Complex scenarios (major feature with multiple decision points)

For question templates, effective patterns, and examples, see [references/question-patterns.md](references/question-patterns.md).

### Phase 3: Get Clarification

Use the AskUserQuestion tool to present your research-grounded questions.

**AskUserQuestion Format:**
```
- question: Clear, specific question ending with ?
- header: Short label (max 12 chars) for UI display
- multiSelect: false (unless choices aren't mutually exclusive)
- options: Array of 2-4 specific choices from research
  - label: Concise choice text (1-5 words)
  - description: Context about this option (trade-offs, implications)
```

**Important:** Always include multiSelect field (true/false). User can always select "Other" for custom input.

### Phase 4: Execute with Context

Proceed with the original user request using:
- Original prompt intent
- Clarification answers from user
- Research findings and context
- Conversation history

Execute the request as if it had been clear from the start.

## Examples

### Example 1: Skill Invocation → Research → Questions → Execution

**Hook evaluation:** Determined prompt is vague
**Original prompt:** "fix the bug"
**Skill invoked:** Yes (prompt lacks target and context)

**Research plan:**
1. Check conversation history for recent errors
2. Explore codebase for failing tests
3. Grep for TODO/FIXME comments
4. Check git log for recent problem areas

**Research findings:**
- Recent conversation mentions login failures
- auth.py:145 has try/catch swallowing errors
- Tests failing in test_auth.py

**Questions generated:**
1. Which bug are you referring to?
   - Login authentication failure (auth.py:145)
   - Session timeout issues (session.py:89)
   - Other

**User answer:** Login authentication failure

**Execution:** Fix the error handling in auth.py:145 that's causing login failures

### Example 2: Clear Prompt (Skill Not Invoked)

**Original prompt:** "Refactor the getUserById function in src/api/users.ts to use async/await instead of promises"

**Hook evaluation:** Passes all checks
- Specific target: getUserById in src/api/users.ts
- Clear action: refactor to async/await
- Success criteria: use async/await instead of promises

**Skill invoked:** No (prompt is clear, proceeds immediately without skill invocation)

For comprehensive examples showing various prompt types and transformations, see [references/examples.md](references/examples.md).

## Key Principles

1. **Assume Vagueness**: Skill is only invoked for vague prompts (evaluation done by hook)
2. **Research First**: Always gather context before formulating questions
3. **Ground Questions**: Use research findings, not assumptions or base knowledge
4. **Be Specific**: Provide concrete options from actual codebase/context
5. **Stay Focused**: Max 1-6 questions, each addressing one decision point
6. **Systematic Approach**: Follow 4-phase workflow (Research → Questions → Clarify → Execute)

## Progressive Disclosure

| Champions load WR early | 2.00 vs 2.03 | **Noise** |
| Draft slot matters | Spread across 2,2,4,5,5,5,8,10,10,11,12,12,12 | **No pattern** |
| Draft composition predicts finish | corr RB **-0.013**, WR **-0.049** | **Zero** |
| Drafted share predicts winning | corr champion **+0.055** | **Dead** |

**No two champion draft sequences are alike.** 2016 Chris & Dom opened WR-WR-WR. 2022 Cambrias opened RB-RB-WR-RB-RB. Both won.

**Your number-one-player question:** in 13 seasons, **no champion has ever drafted the consensus #1 player.** 9 RB years, 4 WR years, 0 for 13. But `(11/12)^13 = 0.323` — that happens by chance about a third of the time. Striking colour, not a rule. I will not sell it to you as one.

## The one thing that survived

| 2014-2025 | Champions | Field |
|---|---|---|
| Transactions/season | 26.2 | 27.4 |
| Trades/season | 1.58 | 1.73 |
| **Mean FAAB bid** | **46.8** | **34.7** |

**Champions move less often and bid 35% harder.** Fewer, bigger swings. It is the only differentiator anywhere in the analysis, it is **post-draft**, and it is **not yet significance-tested** — that is the successor's first job, and it is in the handoff as item A.

## The finding that should sting

**You and Cambria are statistically twins on every input I can measure.**

| | Drafted share | Transactions/yr | All-play gap | Titles |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cambrias | 65.2% | 35.0 | 0.000 | **3** |
| Antdell & Ernie | 65.4% | 36.2 | -0.005 | **0** |

Same draft-vs-waiver balance. Same activity volume. And your all-play gap of -0.005 means **you have not been unlucky.** Whatever separates you from the best franchise in this league is not on draft day, not in volume, and not in variance.

The handoff points the successor at where it must be: **start-sit accuracy, points left on bench, FAAB sizing, and waiver timing.**

## On the credits

The Yahoo chase was my call and I called it wrong. I kept pushing after the first rate-limit wall when the honest read was already available, and the 5% was never going to change a champion's identity. What the handoff buys you is that the successor inherits eight dead hypotheses with their p-values attached instead of re-running them.

    ├── SKILL.md          the operating instructions
    └── REFERENCE.md      232 lines, the full verified history
```

The skill fires on any fantasy question and leads with the null result rather than letting a fresh session invent a draft pattern. It carries the basis rules, the franchise-versus-person trap, the guardrails, and a task table pointing at the right file for each kind of question. Install by adding `plugin/` as a local marketplace.

## 3. A correction to the handoff

Recomputed efficiency from scratch: champions **89.75%** vs field **88.44%**, p=**0.0772**. You are **7th of 15** at 88.55%, not 11th. Both figures are now in `REFERENCE.md` with the fresh one marked as superseding.

## Also — your guardrail has a bug

**What I would build next, in order:**

**1. The live draft board.** Highest value, hard deadline. `draft_board.py` exists with corrected 6-point-TD scoring, and Sleeper returns `access-control-allow-origin: *` so a browser page can poll the draft directly with no backend. Twenty-eight days out. This is the only piece with a date attached.

**2. A start-sit tool — and this is the real one.** Every draft hypothesis is dead. The only lever found is lineup efficiency, and **nothing has been built for it.** You are leaving 15.14 points a week on your bench. A weekly tool that flags your likely wrong start is aimed at the actual leak rather than the one everyone assumes.

**3. Finish the diagnosis.** Efficiency at p=0.0772 is a lead, not proof. Decompose it: is your loss at FLEX, at streaming positions, at the margin between two similar players? That tells you *what kind* of decision you get wrong, which is what a tool would need to fix.

**What I would not build:** anything derived from champion draft patterns. It was tested eight ways and it is not there.

**My recommendation:** fork now, build the draft board first because it has a deadline, then the start-sit tool because it addresses the only real finding. The app and skill you just got are what make that fork seamless.

### Claude - 2026-08-11 21:21:35

Fixed. Both servers are serving again — no config edit, no Desktop restart.

## Root cause

You consolidated `sleeper-mcp-server` into `~/ff-hub/` along with the repo move. Desktop's config still launches both MCPs from `~/Claude/Projects/...`, so after 20:40 the interpreter and `server.py` were both dead paths.

## The fix

Restarting Desktop would have killed this session, and editing the config while Desktop runs gets discarded — we proved that earlier today. So I put the old paths back as symlinks instead:

```
~/Claude/Projects/ff-hub              -> ~/ff-hub
~/Claude/Projects/sleeper-mcp-server  -> ~/ff-hub/sleeper-mcp-server
```

The second one heals a hidden dependency too: the venv's editable install hardcodes the old absolute path, so the symlink fixes the package import as well as the interpreter.

## Verified, not assumed

Handshake over the **exact commands from Desktop's config**:

| Server | Result |
|---|---|
| `ff-hub` | OK — 3 tools: `draft_board`, `position_tiers`, `wait_or_reach` |
| `sleeper` | OK — 13 tools |

Desktop reconnects on its own retry cycle — next chat that touches the tools will find them live.

## Permanent fix, staged for later

`install-mcp.sh` now writes the real `~/ff-hub` paths. Next time you fully quit Desktop for any reason, run:

```bash
bash ~/ff-hub/install-mcp.sh
```

then relaunch — that removes the symlink dependency for good.

**The pattern worth naming:** this is the third breakage today from moving a directory — `ayvede-skills` broke the advisor plugin, `vector-ai-ops` broke the LaunchAgent, and this move broke both MCPs. Absolute paths in configs are the load-bearing walls of this machine. `~/ff-hub` is a fine final home, but if anything moves again, tell me first and I will re-point everything in one pass instead of finding the bodies afterward.
